### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/data-model-rules.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**17** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b6e870707b95d7b8ee9cedd68ad358b51de0da91`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/data-model-rules.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b6e870707b95d7b8ee9cedd68ad358b51de0da91` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9257c896a011041963a0e28e15125ed061f77193` — the merge of head `e71d385be010b036a4315bf7d8625d9ac8d2a274` into base `b6e870707b95d7b8ee9cedd68ad358b51de0da91`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9257c896a011041963a0e28e15125ed061f77193 && git checkout 9257c896a011041963a0e28e15125ed061f77193
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b6e870707b95d7b8ee9cedd68ad358b51de0da91 e71d385be010b036a4315bf7d8625d9ac8d2a274 && git checkout -B drift-repro b6e870707b95d7b8ee9cedd68ad358b51de0da91 && git merge --no-ff e71d385be010b036a4315bf7d8625d9ac8d2a274

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b6e870707b95d7b8ee9cedd68ad358b51de0da91
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b6e870707b95d7b8ee9cedd68ad358b51de0da91` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

**The rule, as the PR states it.** A `controlled_by_parent` object whose one required `master_detail` carries `readonly: true` or `system: true` is refused at parse, at `fields`, naming the object, the field and each flag. Governing text: ADR-0055 §1 and §3, ADR-0087, ruling 6328204856 route A. Prescription: drop the flag and declare the master reference as an ordinary required field; rows that must outlive their parent belong to an object with its own `sharingModel`.

Each accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, judged:

1. **One predicate, every parse door narrowed by one shape — right.** `controlledByParentMasterRefusal` (controlled-by-parent-master.ts) gains the branch for exactly one counting master whose definition carries either flag `=== true`. Read in the cited code, that predicate is the only judge at: `ObjectSchema`'s refinement `refuseControlledByParentWithoutOneMaster` (object.zod.ts), which covers `.parse`, `.safeParse` and `create()` (the builder ends in `ObjectSchemaBase.parse`); `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema.objects` (so `defineStack`, `os validate`, `os build`); the metadata save door (`METADATA_TYPE_SCHEMAS.object` is `ObjectSchema`); and the objectExtensions merge check in stack.zod.ts, which calls the same predicate on the base fields and on the merged map with no code change. No second copy exists: the lint rule is not wired into `AUTHORING_RULES` and the builder's `forceCbpMasterDetailRequired` reads neither flag (its docblock now says so). Ruling item 2's rejections of B, C and D are honoured: nothing under packages/objectql or packages/plugins moves.

2. **The flags are read `=== true` only — right.** `FieldSchema` declares `readonly` as `z.boolean().default(false)` and `system` as optional, so on the parsed map and on a stored body the same verdict is reached; an explicit `readonly: false` / `system: false` is accepted, and the tests pin it.

3. **`isControlledByParentMasterField` unchanged — right.** The runtime's master resolver counts `master_detail` + `required` and nothing else (security-plugin.ts, the resolver's own predicate since #23100), so a flagged required master is still the resolved master, and a flagged one beside a second required one is still two masters; the parse and the runtime keep counting one set. The plugin's other read of the two flags serves a different question (whether record validation covers an omitted reference) and is not the resolver, so the PR's "no runtime change" claim holds as read.

4. **Public surface of `@objectstack/spec/data` — right, and declared.** `ControlledByParentMasterShape` gains the member `master-not-writable`; the predicate returns a refusal at path `fields` for a shape it previously accepted. No new export, no new authorable key or value, and the api-surface artifact records a type's existence only, so no generated artifact moves. The one in-tree exhaustive consumer of the shape (refused-shapes.ts) gains its case in the same diff.

5. **Stored-row listing — right.** refused-shapes.ts lists a stored object in the shape once under `cbp-master-relation-tiers-retired`, rewrites nothing, and its fate text for this shape no longer claims a runtime denial (the module's "one judge, two readers" invariant holds: listed exactly when the parse refuses). The non-null assertion on `masterDetails.find(...)` is safe: the same fields map produced a refusal with exactly one counting master.

6. **ADR-0087 kit — the step-18 D3 entry is amended rather than paralleled; the lint-promotion entry is corrected where this change made it false.** Right as a method: `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md` carries the same form repeatedly (a pre-existing step-18 entry amended in the diff, disposed `already-registered`), and the listing already reports this rule under that id. ⛔ One sentence of the amended entry is now false, see FAIL item 1 under ③.

7. **Lint package — right.** `relationship/master-detail-required` is unchanged in reach (the `os lint` sweep and the rubric); its docblock and `os explain` text now say which shapes the parse refuses and which are the rule's alone; the test file flips the two builder cases to pin the builder's refusal and the rule's report on the literal.

8. **Tests — right for the claims they pin.** Spec: six new shapes agree between the export and `ObjectSchema`, the refusal names object, field and every flag, `create()` refuses with one issue at `fields`, the unflagged control builds. Conversions: one TODO, not rewritten, same parse key, no denial claim. Metadata-protocol: the save door answers 422 `INVALID_METADATA` at `fields` and stores nothing, control saves; its engine double is pinned in scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json.

9. **Producer search (ruling item 3) — in-repo half confirmed, HotCRM half not.** Re-read at the head: every non-test `controlled_by_parent` declarant (examples/app-crm, examples/app-showcase, the CLI lint corpus) declares its master without either flag; no YAML/JSON metadata declares the model. HotCRM is not readable from this session either (the repository is not enabled; a read answers 403), so that half of the ruling's first act stands unmeasured by both the dev and this review — FAIL item 2 under ③.

10. **Governed surfaces — none.** No path under docs/adr, .claude, skills, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or .github/workflows; the Governed Surface Queue Guard check-run is `success`.

**Check-runs on the head (their conclusions are the gate verdicts).** `success`: Auto Label, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, No other open PR may claim the same issue, No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path, Part-of PR must not also close its card, Spec property liveness, The card this PR closes must claim this branch, Type Check · source gates, filter. `in_progress` at this read (reported as pending, not waited for): Build Core, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Test Core (1/6 to 6/6), Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · workspace. `skipped` (opt-in or main-only): 18.x upgrade harness, Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Regression Gate shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance. Three required contexts (Build Core, Test Core, Type Check · workspace, which holds the spec generated-artifact gates) are among the pending ones.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/25092-cbp-master-writable.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `@objectstack/lint: patch`. **Right.** The kind is `narrowed` (a declaration the parse accepted is refused), which takes at least `minor` on a package whose published source the diff moves; spec carries it. The lint move is explanation and docblock text under its `src/**` and the level axis asks for at least one package at `minor`, so `patch` on lint stands. packages/metadata-protocol moves a test file only and scripts/ publishes nothing: no entry owed. Check Changeset is `success`.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and in the changeset: **true.** No published accept set widens and no new export, key or accepted value appears; the one additive type member (item ① 4) rides on an existing public discriminant and is declared in the body. `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`: **true.** The `**BREAKING**` banner, the FROM → TO block and the one-line fix are in the changeset body, as a breaking changeset must carry.
- ADR-0087 disposition marker: `not-required (already-registered cbp-master-relation-tiers-retired)`. **Admitted and honest in the form the repository already uses:** the id pre-dates the merge base, the entry is amended in this diff to carry the new shape, and the stored-row listing reports under it. The marker's reason reads "already carries this narrowing; its text is updated in this change" — accurate at the head, and the precedent wording ("registered before this change, amended in this diff") is the clearer spelling if the changeset is touched for FAIL item 1.
- Ships in 18.x with no retirement stage, under the maintainer's standing line the ruling quotes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev open question — register under the existing parse entry (A) or a new step-18 entry (B)?** Answered: **A.** It is the same parse rule, the same predicate and the id the listing already reports under; `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md` records the same choice for other amended step-18 entries. B would give one rule two ledger ids, and the listing can name only one.
- **Dev flag: HotCRM not measured.** Escalated, and a condition of PASS: FAIL item 2.
- **Dev flag: the plugin-security test file calls the two flagged fixtures "authorable" (stale word, outside the claim's surface, carrier none).** Accepted as noted: the suite registers raw against an unchanged runtime and measures what it says.
- **Dev flag: a flag on a second, non-required `master_detail` beside the master stays the lint rule's report alone.** Accepted: ADR-0055 §1 decides on the one master; the entry and the explanation say so.
- **Dev flag: `os lint` double-reports the flagged shape beside the parse's refusal.** Accepted as the existing state for a missing `required` too; noted in the acceptance notes.
- **Disclosure.** The PR body and changeset state the declaration rule, its governing text, its prescription and the authoring doors the parse reaches, and name no request, write door or served value beyond what the card and ruling already state. Within the ruling; nothing to redact.

**FAIL items** (what a PASS record on the next head needs):

1. **The amended step-18 entry `18.cbp-master-relation-tiers-retired.ts` now contradicts the diff's own fate text for the new shape.** Its `acceptanceCriteria` says a stored row "in any other retired shape still registers … and is denied until it is corrected and saved", then adds "a master marked `readonly` or `system`" to the list of such rows — while refused-shapes.ts and object.zod.ts in the same diff say that shape is NOT denied at runtime (the master still resolves; what it loses is the save door). The entry is the upgrade guide's and the package-shipped guide's source text, so this publishes a denial the runtime does not perform (Prime Directive 10, ADR-0049). Fix: scope the "is denied" clause to the shapes that lose their master and state the flagged shape's fate as the listing does (registers under its diagnostic; the save door refuses it until corrected). Same file, one sentence; re-read the `replacement` sentence "the runtime derives no master from them" for the same ambiguity while there.
2. **Ruling 6328204856 item 3 names HotCRM in the producer search, and it is unmeasured.** Not a defect of the diff — the repository is unreachable from the dev's container and from this session — but the ruling's first act is incomplete. Before the next record: a seat with HotCRM read access posts on #25092 the census (the tree sha and the count of `controlled_by_parent` declarants whose master carries either flag; a producer found is reported as a fork, not pushed over), or the maintainer waives that half. The in-repo half is confirmed here.
